## Simulations for EA and BIP

Question:

if we have a BIP PRS (3% of variance in BIP) and a stronger EA PRS (12% of variance in EA\< about 60% of that within sibs), what are our expectations on power if we regress BIP on the EA PRS vs EA on the BIP PRS?

This should help you get started!

```{r}

# write into a loop, test how many times p < 0.05

# N of 20 k pairs?

N <- 40000

# assume effetc EA -> BIP: .2 (feel free to change!)

rg <- .2

# assumed R2 for the PRS, update to better guesses from the literature:

R2EA <- .06
R2BIP <- .015


PRS_EA <- rnorm(N,0,1)

EA <- sqrt(R2EA) * PRS_EA + sqrt(1-R2EA)*rnorm(N,0,1)


PRS_BIP <- rnorm(N,0,1)

BIP <- sqrt(R2BIP)*PRS_BIP + sqrt(1-R2BIP)*rnorm(N,0,1) 

cor(BIP,PRS_BIP)^2

BIP2 <- .1*EA + BIP
EA2 <- .1*BIP + EA


# BIP is binary with prevalence ~1%, so:

BIP_bin <- as.numeric(scale(BIP2) > qnorm(.99))


## check power...

summary(glm(BIP_bin ~ PRS_EA))

summary(lm(EA2 ~ PRS_BIP))


```

```{r}


### POWER (Regressing EA PRS on BIP)

set.seed(123)

rep <- 1000 ##how many times to repeat the analysis 
output1 <- matrix(NA,nrow=rep,ncol=2)

for (i in 1:rep) 
  { 

N <- 40000

rg <- .2

# assumed R2 for the PRS
R2EA <- .15
R2BIP <- .05


PRS_EA <- rnorm(N,0,1)

EA <- sqrt(R2EA) * PRS_EA + sqrt(1-R2EA)*rnorm(N,0,1)

PRS_BIP <- rnorm(N,0,1)

BIP <- sqrt(R2BIP)*PRS_BIP + sqrt(1-R2BIP)*rnorm(N,0,1) 

BIP2 <- .1*EA + BIP
EA2 <- .1*BIP + EA

#EA2 <- EA2 - .3*BIP_bin this is if tgetting bip actually harms your education!

# BIP is binary with prevalence ~1%, so:
BIP_bin <- as.numeric(scale(BIP2) > qnorm(.99))

dataf <- cbind.data.frame(PRS_EA, PRS_BIP, EA2, BIP_bin)

  reg1 <- glm(BIP_bin ~ PRS_EA, data=dataf) 
  
  output1[i,] <- summary(reg1)$coef[2,c(1,4)] 
  # save the estimate beta and p-value for the beta 
  
  
  
}

hist(output1[,1]) # histogram of estimated beta's abline(v=beta,col="red",lwd=2) # with the true beta as a red line

sum(output1[,2] < 0.05)/rep  ##Power - the proportion of tests that are significant 

### POWER (regressing BP PRS on EA)

set.seed(123)

rep <- 1000 ##how many times to repeat the analysis 
output2 <- matrix(NA,nrow=rep,ncol=2)

for (i in 1:rep) 
{ 
N <- 40000

rg <- .2

# assumed R2 for the PRS
R2EA <- .15
R2BIP <- .05


PRS_EA <- rnorm(N,0,1)

EA <- sqrt(R2EA) * PRS_EA + sqrt(1-R2EA)*rnorm(N,0,1)

PRS_BIP <- rnorm(N,0,1)

BIP <- sqrt(R2BIP)*PRS_BIP + sqrt(1-R2BIP)*rnorm(N,0,1) 

BIP2 <- .1*EA + BIP
EA2 <- .1*BIP + EA


# BIP is binary with prevalence ~1%, so:
BIP_bin <- as.numeric(scale(BIP2) > qnorm(.99))

#EA2 <- EA2 - .3*BIP_bin

dataf <- cbind.data.frame(PRS_EA, PRS_BIP, EA2, BIP_bin)
  
  reg2 <- lm(EA2 ~ PRS_BIP, data=dataf) 
  output2[i,] <- summary(reg2)$coef[2,c(1,4)] # save the estimate beta and p-value for the beta 
  }

hist(output2[,1]) # histogram of estimated beta's abline(v=beta,col="red",lwd=2) # with the true beta as a red line

sum(output2[,2] < 0.05)/rep  ##Power - proportion of tests that are significant

```
